# Documentation conventions (`doc/`)

`doc/` is the user-facing reference. The docs site publishes it verbatim at each release tag under `https://anilcancakir.com/magic/docs/devtools/<section>/<page>` (and the same URL with `.md`), and an agent reads one page at a time, so every page stands alone.

## Layout

- Pages live at `doc/<section>/<page>.md`: two levels, lowercase `[a-z0-9-]` names, sections `getting-started`, `basics` and `guides`. There is no `doc/index.md`, because the site skips files outside that shape.
- API dumps, changelog entries, marketing copy and internal architecture stay out of `doc/`; they belong to dartdoc, `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md`.

## Page shape

- The H1 is the first line and the only H1. The sentence after it says what the page is, since the site copies it as the page description in its generated `llms.txt`.
- A bare bullet list of `#slug` links follows the lead, one per `##` section, and `<a name="slug"></a>` sits on the line right before every `##`.
- Open with the answer (a minimal sample or a Quick Reference table), then explain. State defaults, limits and failure modes on the page.
- A `basics` page carries a Gotchas table (mistake, fix) of three to six rows, each traceable to a line in `lib/`.
- Every page ends with `## Related Documentation`, linking siblings by relative `.md` path; a link that leaves `doc/` 404s on the site.
- Tables are left-aligned (`|:---|`) with every identifier in backticks.

## Samples and claims

- Dart samples use `dart` fences, shell commands `bash`. A sample carries its imports and compiles as written: paste it into a scratch file inside the package, run `flutter analyze` on it, then delete the file.
- Check every count, key name, threshold and command name against `lib/` and the resolved `tapir`, `crumbs` and `magic` sources before it goes on a page; an agent acts on those details literally.
- Name the products `tapir`, `crumbs`, `dowel` and `wind_kit`.

## Verify

Run `python3 tool/check-docs.py` before calling doc work done; CI runs the same script in the `Internal Links` job.
